sets.notes: npm run is allowed because scripts are repository code running inside the sandbox. Install scripts stay disabled and installs only happen in fetch_deps.
Held only by the specification_writer role (tools.entries exec.run, role_scopes). Network is off in the agent profile whatever the script does.

never_allow_from_sandbox.reason: git push, gist and repository creation are exfiltration channels; the control plane clones and pushes
token theft would become repository write access

allow.justification: crate metadata API, read by the control plane's registry client for the dependency gates

forbidden_command_classes.description: Shell strings defeat argv-level policy. Use typed commands instead.
Download and run, or pipe a download into an interpreter.
Raw network clients, tunnels and DNS tools. Network is denied anyway; this catches attempts early.
Agents never push or rewrite history. The control plane owns every push.

Spec Kit is confined to the specification stage and its four skills. These subcommands install, upgrade, reach the network or run the full workflow. The control plane runs `specify init` and `specify integration status --json` on the host; an agent never does.
Processes that outlive the tool call. The wrapper also kills the whole process group at call end.

Package installs and downloads may run only in the fetch_deps profile. Inside that profile the command sets decide which of them exist: `cargo fetch` and `cargo metadata` for Slice 1, no install, add, update or vendor, and the next class keeps repository code out.

The fetch_deps profile downloads and runs no repository code: no build script, procedural macro, test binary, project script or interpreter, because it is the one profile with a network. Applies to fetch_deps only (the other two profiles are excepted).

non_overridable_blocks.reason: The block waits for a recorded human decision bound to the exact name, version and checksum; an override would pass the stage with none.
waits for a security approver's decision on new build code
waits for a person with the approver designation to apply the label of the approved design; an override would start work with no such label on the issue

semantic_checks.description: lint level lowered, allow attributes added, ignore lists grown
harness=false, test targets removed, ignore or skip markers, conftest hooks that deselect
new build.rs, setup.py, postinstall or similar
alternate registry, git or path dependency, patch or replace section
privileged, host network, new capabilities, exposed ports in container or IaC changes

groups.reason: CI definitions and code ownership decide what runs and who reviews.
Lint, type, coverage and scanner settings, and the CI entry point (scripts/ci.sh and scripts/ci/), decide what a PASS means.
Project-local factory configuration and Spec Kit state. Changed only through the specification and configuration stages.
Files that steer future agent runs. A builder editing them is persistent prompt injection.
Hooks and submodule pointers run or fetch code on developer machines and on the control plane.
Existing fixtures and golden files may be added to but not edited or removed to force a pass.
Builders add tests; they do not weaken or remove existing ones. Rewrites need spec authorization and independent policy review.
Held-out evaluation data must never be visible to builders or reach model context.
Never mounted, never read into context, never allowed in a diff. Hidden at any depth, not only at the repository root.
When the factory works on its own repository, its policies, security documents and agent manifests are protected.
When the factory works on its own repository, the tools and test oracles that its gates run are protected, as the CI entry point and the gate configuration are.

agent.purpose: Agent CLI and its tool execution. Reaches only the model broker.

fetch_deps.purpose: Download dependencies with install scripts disabled. Runs no repository code.

verify.purpose: Trusted build, test and scan gates. Fresh container per gate run.

entries.notes: Writes go through path_access and protected_paths. Atomic temp-file plus rename. A role scope narrows further and never widens: a path must pass the scope, the task's owned files and the protected paths.
In fetch_deps the commands are chosen by the supervisor after the dependency decision, not requested by an agent. The same wrapper and command_sets apply.

entries.description: status, diff, log, show against the host-side trusted git directory.
Control plane commits the workspace to the job branch with a hardened git environment.

Typed dependency request. With the agent CLI inside the sandbox this is a field of the agent's structured result, not a mediated call. A human decides every new direct dependency; a fetch_deps run follows only on approval.
Factory-side fetch through the SSRF guard (see untrusted_content.web_fetch). Never available to builders.
Structured, schema-validated output channel. The only way an agent returns results.

required_flags: --model <the explicit model of the manifest's recommended_models>
claude_code.tools_flag: --tools=, --allowedTools=, --disallowedTools= from the manifest and the grants

codex_cli.env_policy: the credential is never an environment variable: it is read from /run/factory/job-token by the provider's auth command, because Codex passes its whole environment, a key variable included, to the shell the model drives (spike 4.5)
required_flags: -m <the explicit model of the manifest's recommended_models>
-c model_providers.factory_broker={name="factory_broker", base_url="<sidecar address>/v1", wire_api="responses", supports_websockets=false, auth={command="cat", args=["/run/factory/job-token"]}}
